checks.label: USB Debugging Enabled
checks.description: USB debugging should be disabled in production
checks.remediation: Disable USB debugging via 'settings put global adb_enabled 0' or in Developer Options.

checks.label: USB File Transfer Disabled
checks.description: Should be disabled to block unauthorized USB file access. Null means not configured (safe default).
checks.remediation: Disable USB file transfer via 'settings put global usb_mass_storage_enabled 0'.

checks.label: USB Mass Storage
checks.description: Check USB configuration mode. ADB mode is expected during audit.
checks.remediation: Set USB mode to charging-only via 'setprop sys.usb.config charging' when not auditing.

checks.label: Connected USB Devices Count
checks.description: USB device count - unexpected devices may indicate BadUSB or hardware keylogger
checks.remediation: Physically inspect and disconnect any unknown USB devices. Audit connected peripherals.

checks.label: USB Accessory Mode
checks.description: Current USB state. ADB mode is expected during audit.
checks.remediation: Switch USB state to charging-only after audit via 'setprop sys.usb.config charging'.

checks.label: MTP Enabled
checks.remediation: Disable MTP via 'settings put global mtp_enabled 0' to prevent file transfer over USB.

checks.label: Serial Device Files Exposed
checks.description: Serial interfaces exposed to userspace - may allow debug console access if physical UART connected
checks.remediation: Restrict serial device permissions or disable unused UART interfaces in the kernel config.

checks.label: GPIO Sysfs Exposed
checks.description: GPIO pins exported to userspace - apps can control hardware pins
checks.remediation: Unexport unused GPIO pins via 'echo <pin> > /sys/class/gpio/unexport' and restrict sysfs permissions.

checks.label: I2C Bus Exposed
checks.description: I2C bus accessible from userspace - can communicate with sensors/peripherals
checks.remediation: Restrict /dev/i2c-* permissions to root or remove kernel I2C chardev support if unused.

checks.label: SPI Bus Exposed
checks.remediation: Restrict /dev/spidev* permissions to root or disable SPI chardev support in the kernel.

checks.label: USB Gadget Controller
checks.description: USB device controller present - device can act as USB peripheral
checks.remediation: Disable USB gadget mode in kernel config if the device should not act as a USB peripheral.

checks.label: Kernel Console Enabled
checks.description: Kernel boot console configured - debug output on serial port
checks.remediation: Remove 'console=' parameters from kernel cmdline in the bootloader config for production builds.

checks.label: Video Capture Devices
checks.command: P=$(ls -d /dev/video* 2>/dev/null); if [ -n "$P" ]; then printf '%s\n' "$P"; elif ls -d /dev/video* 2>&1 | grep -qi 'permission denied'; then echo UNMEASURED; else echo "ABSENT no video capture device"; fi
checks.remediation: Restrict /dev/video* permissions and disable unused camera drivers in the kernel config.

checks.label: Audio Capture Devices
checks.command: P=$(ls -d /dev/snd/pcm*c* 2>/dev/null); if [ -n "$P" ]; then printf '%s\n' "$P"; elif ls -d /dev/snd/pcm*c* 2>&1 | grep -qi 'permission denied'; then echo UNMEASURED; else echo "ABSENT no audio capture device"; fi
checks.remediation: Restrict /dev/snd/ permissions and disable unused audio capture drivers if not needed.

checks.label: Raw Memory Access
checks.description: /dev/mem or /dev/kmem exposed - allows raw memory read/write!
checks.remediation: Remove /dev/mem and /dev/kmem by disabling CONFIG_DEVMEM and CONFIG_DEVKMEM in the kernel.

checks.label: Block Devices Writable
checks.remediation: Set block device permissions to root-only (chmod 600) to prevent unauthorized disk access.

checks.label: USB-C Port Roles and Power Delivery
checks.command: P=$(ls -d /sys/class/typec/port* 2>/dev/null | head -4); if [ -z "$P" ]; then echo NO_TYPEC_SYSFS; else O=''; for d in $P; do r=$(cat $d/data_role 2>/dev/null | tr -d '\n'); p=$(cat $d/power_role 2>/dev/null | tr -d '\n'); O="$O $(basename $d):data=${r:-?},power=${p:-?}"; done; echo "TYPEC_PRESENT$O"; fi
checks.description: Reports the USB-C port data and power roles. A port in dual-role or host mode negotiates Power Delivery with whatever is attached, and the PD message parser runs in the USB-C controller firmware below the operating system, which is the surface behind the BadPower class of attacks where a malicious charger rewrites controller firmware. A port acting as host also enumerates attacker-supplied devices, reaching every USB class driver in the kernel. Informational because dual-role is the normal configuration on a phone; on a fixed-function device it is often unnecessary.
checks.remediation: On a POS terminal, kiosk or embedded device that only charges, pin the port to sink and device role so it neither sources power nor enumerates attached peripherals, and disable USB host mode in the kernel configuration.

checks.label: USB Video Class Driver Binding Surface
checks.command: V=$(uname -r 2>/dev/null); C=""; OBS=0; if [ -r /proc/config.gz ]; then C=$(zcat /proc/config.gz 2>/dev/null | grep "^CONFIG_USB_VIDEO_CLASS="); OBS=1; fi; if [ -z "$C" ] && [ -n "$V" ] && [ -r "/boot/config-$V" ]; then C=$(grep "^CONFIG_USB_VIDEO_CLASS=" < "/boot/config-$V" 2>/dev/null); OBS=1; fi; if [ -z "$C" ] && [ -r /proc/config ]; then C=$(grep "^CONFIG_USB_VIDEO_CLASS=" < /proc/config 2>/dev/null); OBS=1; fi; L=$(grep -cE "^(uvcvideo) " /proc/modules 2>/dev/null | head -1); L=${L:-0}; D=$(find /vendor/lib/modules /vendor_dlkm/lib/modules /system/lib/modules /system_dlkm/lib/modules /odm/lib/modules /lib/modules -maxdepth 4 \( -name "uvcvideo.ko" \) 2>/dev/null | head -2 | tr "\n" " "); if [ "$L" != "0" ]; then echo "uvc_driver=ENABLED basis=loaded modules=$L"; exit 0; fi; case "$C" in *=y) echo "uvc_driver=ENABLED basis=builtin $C"; exit 0;; *=m) echo "uvc_driver=ENABLED basis=module $C"; exit 0;; esac; if [ -n "$D" ]; then echo "uvc_driver=ENABLED basis=ondisk $D"; exit 0; fi; if [ "$OBS" = "0" ] && [ ! -r /proc/modules ]; then echo "UNMEASURED kernel config unreadable and /proc/modules unreadable"; exit 0; fi; if [ "$OBS" = "0" ]; then echo "NOT_OBSERVABLE kernel config not readable, driver not loaded, no module file found"; exit 0; fi; echo "uvc_driver=DISABLED basis=config"
checks.description: Scores whether the USB Video Class driver will bind a camera an attacker plugs in. CVE-2024-53104, in the CISA exploited catalog since 2025-02-05, is an out-of-bounds write in uvc_parse_streaming parsing descriptors supplied by the attached device, and it is reached by physical access rather than from software on the device. This is a different property from the existing Video Capture Devices check, which inventories the /dev/video nodes that exist right now, is info level with a match-anything pattern, and so can never raise a finding; a device with no camera has no such node yet still binds a hostile USB camera the moment one is attached. Evidence comes from the kernel config, the loaded module list and the on-disk module file, because uvcvideo is normally tristate and autoloads on device attach. On a general-purpose phone that supports USB webcams this reports the surface as present and that is expected. The finding is aimed at fixed-function builds, kiosk, point of sale, panel and medical devices, where no USB camera is ever legitimately attached.
checks.remediation: On a fixed-function device, build without CONFIG_USB_VIDEO_CLASS, or blacklist uvcvideo and disable USB host mode so no descriptor from an attached device is parsed. Where USB cameras must work, restrict USB data while the device is locked so descriptors are not parsed before authentication.
checks.why: Descriptor parsing happens before any authentication, so a malicious USB device reaches kernel code with the screen locked.
checks.risk_if_fail: Kernel memory corruption from physical access, the primitive used in forensic unlock chains.

checks.label: USB Audio Class Driver Binding Surface
checks.command: V=$(uname -r 2>/dev/null); C=""; OBS=0; if [ -r /proc/config.gz ]; then C=$(zcat /proc/config.gz 2>/dev/null | grep "^CONFIG_SND_USB_AUDIO="); OBS=1; fi; if [ -z "$C" ] && [ -n "$V" ] && [ -r "/boot/config-$V" ]; then C=$(grep "^CONFIG_SND_USB_AUDIO=" < "/boot/config-$V" 2>/dev/null); OBS=1; fi; if [ -z "$C" ] && [ -r /proc/config ]; then C=$(grep "^CONFIG_SND_USB_AUDIO=" < /proc/config 2>/dev/null); OBS=1; fi; L=$(grep -cE "^(snd_usb_audio) " /proc/modules 2>/dev/null | head -1); L=${L:-0}; D=$(find /vendor/lib/modules /vendor_dlkm/lib/modules /system/lib/modules /system_dlkm/lib/modules /odm/lib/modules /lib/modules -maxdepth 4 \( -name "snd-usb-audio.ko" -o -name "snd_usb_audio.ko" \) 2>/dev/null | head -2 | tr "\n" " "); if [ "$L" != "0" ]; then echo "usb_audio_driver=ENABLED basis=loaded modules=$L"; exit 0; fi; case "$C" in *=y) echo "usb_audio_driver=ENABLED basis=builtin $C"; exit 0;; *=m) echo "usb_audio_driver=ENABLED basis=module $C"; exit 0;; esac; if [ -n "$D" ]; then echo "usb_audio_driver=ENABLED basis=ondisk $D"; exit 0; fi; if [ "$OBS" = "0" ] && [ ! -r /proc/modules ]; then echo "UNMEASURED kernel config unreadable and /proc/modules unreadable"; exit 0; fi; if [ "$OBS" = "0" ]; then echo "NOT_OBSERVABLE kernel config not readable, driver not loaded, no module file found"; exit 0; fi; echo "usb_audio_driver=DISABLED basis=config"
checks.description: Scores whether the USB audio class driver will bind a device an attacker plugs in. CVE-2024-53197 and CVE-2024-53150, both in the CISA exploited catalog, are an out-of-bounds access and an out-of-bounds read in the USB audio driver reached through descriptors from the attached device. Like the USB video surface this is a physical-access path and the parsing happens before authentication. Kept separate from the USB Video Class check because the two drivers are configured independently, so a device can ship one without the other and two findings there reflect two real decisions rather than one condition counted twice. Evidence comes from the kernel config, the loaded module list and the on-disk module file, matching both the dash and underscore spellings of the module filename. On a phone, USB-C headsets need this driver and the surface being present is a deliberate tradeoff. The finding is aimed at fixed-function builds where no USB audio device is ever attached.
checks.remediation: On a fixed-function device, build without CONFIG_SND_USB_AUDIO, or blacklist snd-usb-audio and disable USB host mode. Where USB audio must work, restrict USB data while the device is locked.
checks.why: A second pre-authentication descriptor parser reachable from the USB port, independent of the video class driver.
checks.risk_if_fail: Kernel memory corruption or disclosure from physical access.
